R692.note: Switching the cache to own std::string closes the dangling string_view cleanly; matches contract exactly with no other observable change.

R693.note: secrets.randbelow() gives the same numeric range and same failure mode on invalid min/max as the original random.randint().

R694.note: getCanonicalFile() + prefix containment check (with trailing separator guard) correctly blocks traversal while preserving normal downloads.

R695.note: Tika content-sniffing plus an allowlist-derived extension and UUID filename correctly closes the trust-the-header issue and matches the stated contract (server-generated retrievable name).

R696.note: toRealPath() canonicalization plus Path.startsWith() correctly blocks traversal/symlink escape while preserving normal downloads and the existing 404 behavior.

R697.note: Correct parameterized-search API, but the diff renames `filter` to `filterExpr` while the later 'nothing found' branch still references the now-undefined `filter` variable (encodeForHTML(filter)) - the file as given would not compile, silently breaking the whole endpoint.

R698.note: Switching from f-string to %-style logging args produces the byte-identical final log message (Python logging does not strip/escape embedded CR/LF), so the CRLF log-forging vector is not actually closed despite the write-up's claim that 'the logger's output filters prevent log injection'.

R699.note: Changing `i <= n` to `i < n` exactly matches the stated copy-n-elements contract with no side effects.

R700.note: JavaScriptEncoder is the right context-aware encoder, but Encode(string) throws ArgumentNullException on null, and Request.QueryString["q"] returns null when absent (a normal case the original silently handled as an empty string) - this crashes the page for any request without a q parameter, unmentioned in the write-up.

R701.note: Rejecting separators/'.'/'..' in the filename and canonicalizing only the pre-existing base directory closes the realpath-false fallback bug while preserving the documented no-subdirectory save contract.

R702.note: redis-py's hset(mapping=...) correctly closes the RESP command-injection vector, but the function's return value silently changes from raw RESP reply bytes to an integer field count, unmentioned in the write-up.

R703.note: Standard Django raw() %s parameterization, no other observable change.

R704.note: JSON.parse is the standard remediation for node-serialize (which has no safe-mode flag to disable code execution), but any already-issued cookie produced in node-serialize format would now silently parse to an empty profile instead of the real data, and this migration impact is never mentioned.

R705.note: log/slog escapes ASCII control characters (including CR/LF) in attribute values across handlers, genuinely closing the log-forging vector; the format change to structured logging is stated openly.

R706.note: Adds PasswordEncoder.matches() before issuing the token, the standard Spring Security pattern; blocks only the previously-unconditional authentication bypass, no legitimate-path regression.

R707.note: NULL check placed before the first dereference, returning the disabled default exactly as the contract requires.

R708.note: http.DetectContentType + random filename + O_EXCL correctly closes the upload trust issue, but the added http.MaxBytesReader introduces a new hard 20MB cap (previously multipart parsing could spill larger files to disk) that could reject legitimate large attachments - disclosed as an add-on but not analyzed for impact.
